3still owed [...] Will these end up in spam?
:   Nobody can promise inbox placement and we won’t start. What we can say is that everything working against you elsewhere is absent here: the mail leaves your own Gmail on your own domain’s reputation, it’s plain text with no tracking pixel and no link shortener, the wording changes on every touch instead of repeating itself, and follow-ups reply into a thread your client has already engaged with.

Can I use it for things that aren’t documents?
:   Yes. Underneath, it’s a checklist plus a nudge. Firms use it for approvals, answers, analytics access, a signed agreement, a billing contact, “three sites you like and why”. If you can put it on a list, Pesterly will keep asking for it. [...] Do I have to leave the tools I already use?
:   No. Pesterly doesn’t replace your portal, your practice management software or your Drive. It’s the thing that gets clients to actually use them. What your client uploads lands straight in a folder in your own Google Drive, so the files are already where you work and already yours.

How new is this?
:   New, and we’d rather say so than fake it. Pesterly started as a done-for-you service, chasing documents by hand on behalf of firms, and this is that job turned into software. It costs $9 a month. There are no customer logos on this page because there aren’t any yet. When there are, they’ll be real ones.

# Client Document Collection Workflow

A practical workflow for firms that collect client files, chase missing documents, and need a cleaner alternative to scattered email attachments.

IndustryProfessional Services Firms

WorkflowClient document collection

Asset typeWorkflow template

Tool stackClient portal, Secure file upload

Many firms lose time chasing client documents: attachments land in email threads, file names are unclear, required items are missing, and staff have to ask the same follow-up questions repeatedly.

This workflow turns document collection into a structured process. The AI can classify uploads, summarize what is missing, draft reminders, and prepare the client packet, while staff review sensitive, rejected, or unclear files.

results.content:
You are a document collection assistant for [Company Name]. Your job is to: 1. Determine which documents are needed based on the client's profile 2. Send clear, specific requests via the client's preferred channel 3. Accept uploaded documents and classify them 4. Validate document quality and completeness 5. Track collection status and send follow-ups for missing items 6. Extract key data fields and push to [target system] Rules: - Always be specific about what's needed (not "send financial documents" but "your Chase bank statement for October and November 2026, all pages") - When a document fails quality checks, explain exactly what's wrong and what to re-send - Follow up on missing documents after 48 hours, then every 72 hours - Escalate to a human after 3 failed follow-ups or if the [...] Here's how to build an AI agent on OpenClaw that handles document collection end to end — requesting the right files, accepting uploads across channels, classifying and organizing what comes in, flagging what's missing, and following up automatically until the file is complete.

## The Manual Workflow Today (And Why It's Brutal)

Let's map out what actually happens when you need to collect documents from a client. I'll use a mortgage loan file as the example because it's one of the most document-heavy processes, but this applies equally to tax preparation, legal matters, insurance claims, and employee onboarding. [...] ### Step 4: Wire Up the Follow-Up Logic

This is where the real time savings come from. Instead of a human checking the file status and sending reminders, the agent maintains state:

```
Client: John Smith Matter: Mortgage Application #2026-1847 Status: Collection In Progress Received: ✅ W-2 (2026) — received 11/14, validated ✅ Pay stubs (30-day) — received 11/14, validated ✅ Government ID — received 11/15, validated Missing: ❌ Bank statements (2 months) — requested 11/14, reminder sent 11/16 ❌ Tax return (2023) — requested 11/14, no response ❌ Homeowners insurance quote — requested 11/15 Next actions: - Send 2nd reminder for bank statements (due: 11/19) - Send 2nd reminder for tax return (due: 11/19) - Send 1st reminder for insurance quote (due: 11/17) 
```
